text:
maya: Hey team — first day, trying to get kubectl talking to the redwood-dev cluster. I'm on a Mac M1. I merged the kubeconfig from the onboarding doc and ran `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` but I get `exec plugin produced no auth data` and sometimes `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Anyone seen this?

liam: welcome Maya! pinging @eng-infra. Two quick checks: did you run `aws sso login` for the profile in the onboarding email? Also make sure you have aws-cli v2 installed (brew install awscli) — M1 needs the arm64 build.

maya: I ran `aws configure sso` with the profile we were given but I might have skipped the actual `aws sso login`. How should the kubeconfig be wired to the SSO profile?

liam: run `aws sso login --profile redwood-sso` then `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-sso`. That writes an exec plugin entry that calls `aws eks get-token` for you. If you manually merged configs you can accidentally break the exec plugin block.

jordan: also check your kubectl binary arch: `kubectl version --client`. If you installed kubectl with the wrong arch (e.g., an x86 binary) the exec plugin might fail. Brew on M1 should give the right one.

sophia: about the x509 error — open `~/.kube/config` and confirm the `certificate-authority-data` field is intact (long base64 blob). If it got truncated during a manual merge you'll see cert errors. Re-running `aws eks update-kubeconfig` usually fixes that.

maya: Looking at the kubeconfig, the user.exec section points to the `aws` binary with args `eks get-token` etc. After trying `aws sso login` I still saw "exec plugin produced no auth data". Any debug tips?

liam: run `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile redwood-sso` to verify your SSO session. If that errors then the token isn't present. Common flow: run `aws sso login`, then verify sts, then update-kubeconfig. Also check your `KUBECONFIG` env var — if it's pointing to an old file you might be editing the wrong config.

maya: `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile redwood-sso` initially returned AccessDenied (said credentials expired). I did `aws sso login` again, sts returned my account id, re-ran `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-sso` and now `kubectl get ns` works. Woo! Thanks.

sophia: nice. Quick paste of the commands we usually share for Mac M1 new hires: 
```
brew install awscli
aws configure sso
aws sso login --profile redwood-sso
aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-sso
kubectl config use-context redwood-dev
kubectl get pods -n redwood-platform
```

liam: one more note — if you ever see weird exec plugin errors try `which aws` to ensure the path is the brew-installed aws and not an old binary, and `echo $KUBECONFIG` to confirm which file kubectl loads.

infra-bot: reminder — do not commit kubeconfigs or credentials to git or dotfiles.

maya: Resolved for me after the sso login + update-kubeconfig. Appreciate the help :tada: If anything weird crops up I'll DM liam or ping @eng-infra.

sophia: welcome aboard again!`
